  - `test/integration/acme-tpm`'s swtpm fixture (`swtpm_helper_test.go`) provisioned only the TCG-standard EK/Shared-SRK/IAK, so every device-attest-01 swtpm test failed past `CreateAttestedKey`: it parents the certificate key under the Platform SRK and `deviceattest01.Setup` reads the IAK certificate, and swtpm's `Provision()` created neither. `SwtpmConnection.Provision` now also calls `xkmssdk.EnrollSimulatorPlatformSRK` and the new `xkmssdk.ProvisionSimulatorIAKCertificate`, the same helpers `pkg/acme/client/service.openDeviceTPM` uses to provision the in-process simulator, so both provisioning paths share one implementation. The IAK certificate minting code that used to live unexported in `device_tpm.go` moved to `pkg/tpm2/tpm2test.ProvisionIAKCertificate`, re-exported from `sdk/go` next to `EnrollSimulatorPlatformSRK`.
  - Files: `pkg/acme/client/service/{challenge,errors,device_tpm}.go`, `pkg/tpm2/tpm2test/iak_cert.go`, `sdk/go/tpm.go`, `test/integration/acme-tpm/swtpm_helper_test.go`.

## [0.36.0-alpha] - 2026-09-28

### Security

- **In a cluster, a certificate revoked on one node is now refused by every node, and every revocation check fails closed.** Revocation records replicate through the CA's revocation store, but `CA.IsRevoked`, and so `CA.Verify` and `CA.VerifyPeerCertificate`, read only the node's in-memory map. That map is filled at `Load` and by the node's own revocations, so a certificate revoked on node A still verified on node B. CRL generation built from the same map, so node B's regenerated CRL overwrote the shared `crl/<ski>` record without node A's revocations. `IsRevoked` and the OCSP responder now share one read path: the map first, then the store. A hit from the store is cached (revocation is permanent), and a miss is never cached. CRL generation now builds from the store's full record set. Each reader treats only a definite not-found as "not revoked". A store fault is `ErrStorageError`, with the storage cause kept in the chain, and refuses the check. A corrupt record is the new `ErrRevocationRecordCorrupt`, naming its key, and now fails `Load` instead of being skipped with a warning, which had silently un-revoked it. A revocation listing failure aborts CRL generation, and nothing is published. An unreadable previous CRL number fails generation instead of restarting the sequence at 1. `VerifyPeerCertificate` refuses a certificate whose revocation status cannot be read instead of accepting it, and OCSP answers `unknown` (go-xkms#1116).
- **A malformed CTAP2 `setPIN`/`changePIN` request could crash the xkey FIDO2 daemon instead of being refused.** `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_clientpin.go` `decryptPIN` checked only a minimum length on `newPinEnc` before calling `cipher.CBCDecrypter.CryptBlocks`, which panics when its input is not a whole number of AES blocks; a 65-byte (protocol 1) or 81-byte (protocol 2) `newPinEnc` reached that panic with nothing on the CTAP/uhid path to recover it. Separately, a decrypted plaintext starting with `0x00` made the old zero-length check fall through to treating the entire 64-byte buffer as the PIN instead of an empty one. `decryptPIN` now requires `newPinEnc` to be exactly 64 bytes (protocol 1) or exactly 80 bytes -- a 16-byte IV plus 64 bytes of ciphertext -- (protocol 2), refusing any other length with `ErrInvalidParameter` (`CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER`) before `CryptBlocks` runs. The decrypted plaintext is then validated per CTAP 2.1 §6.5.5.5 step 5 by a new `extractPaddedPIN`/`validatePINLength`: the PIN is every byte before the first `0x00` terminator, every byte from the terminator onward must also be `0x00`, and the PIN itself must be non-empty, at most 63 bytes, and at least the configured `minPINLength` in Unicode code points -- every violation, including a buffer with no terminator at all, reports `ErrPINPolicyViolation` (`CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION`). `decryptBlock`'s V2 branch (the `pinHashEnc` decrypt shared by `changePIN`, `getPinToken`, and `getPinUvAuthTokenUsingPinWithPermissions`) is tightened from a minimum to the same exact-length check for CTAP conformance; it already sliced a fixed-size window before `CryptBlocks` so it could not panic. `pin_protocol_v1.go`/`pin_protocol_v2.go` `Decapsulate` and `ext_hmac_secret.go` `decryptSalts` already guarded their `CryptBlocks` calls with an exact or block-multiple length check and needed no change. As defence in depth, `authenticator.go`'s `ProcessCBORWithContext` now dispatches every CTAP2 command through a single recover boundary (`dispatchCommand`/`recoverCommandPanic`): a handler panic is logged with the command byte and a stack trace and reported as the new `ErrCommandPanicked`, which maps to `CTAP2_ERR_OTHER` instead of crashing the daemon. Verified by `xkey/pkg/authenticator/cmd_clientpin_decryptpin_security_test.go` (a table test over the 65/81/63/0-byte lengths confirming none panics and each returns `ErrInvalidParameter`; a well-formed-length ciphertext with a stray non-zero byte after the terminator, a plaintext with no terminator at all, and a leading `0x00` all return `ErrPINPolicyViolation`; a valid PIN still round-trips for both protocols; `FuzzDecryptPIN` seeded with all of the above; and `recoverCommandPanic` mapping a simulated panic to `ErrCommandPanicked`/`StatusOtherError`). go-xkms#1149.
- **The xkey GUI silently disabled TLS certificate pinning (and reset the FIDO2 firmware version) on every settings save.** `services.GUIConfigData` (`xkey/pkg/gui/services/app_service.go:81`), the DTO the Settings screen reads and writes through `AppService.GetConfig`/`UpdateConfig`, had no field for `GUIConfig.ServerSPKIPin` (the hex SPKI pin that lets a first-contact connection trust a server without a CA certificate) or `GUIConfig.FIDO2FirmwareVersion`. The `ConfigUpdater` callback wired in `NewApp` (`xkey/pkg/gui/app.go:2401`) persisted every save by rebuilding a whole new `GUIConfig` from that DTO alone (`dataToConfig`), so any settings change — theme, window size, anything — zeroed both fields in memory and on disk, silently disabling certificate pinning. `dataToConfig` is now `applyDataToConfig` (`app.go:281`): it merges the DTO onto a **copy of the existing** `GUIConfig` instead of rebuilding one, so a field the DTO does not carry is always preserved from the pre-existing config. Neither field gained a Settings UI control — `ServerSPKIPin` is set only via the `gui.server_spki_pin` CLI flag/env or by editing `gui.json` directly, and `FIDO2FirmwareVersion` only once at startup from the build version string — so no new editable surface was added. `TestConfigDataRoundTrip` (`xkey/pkg/gui/config_data_roundtrip_test.go`) walks every exported `GUIConfig` field via reflection and fails the build if a future field is added without either a DTO mapping or a documented entry in `unmappedGUIConfigDataFields`; `TestApplyDataToConfig_PreservesUnrelatedSettingsSave` proves the SPKI pin and firmware version survive an unrelated settings save both in memory and in the file `SaveGUIConfig` writes (go-xkms#1122).
- **With a user store configured, the mTLS authenticator now fails closed: a client certificate that does not resolve to a bound, enabled qrdb user never authenticates.** `pkg/auth/mtls.go` `buildIdentity` used to treat every `UserStore.GetByCertFingerprint` error the same way. Whether the certificate was unbound or the store could not answer (a sealed tenant barrier, a failed index read, an unreachable remote), it built an identity from the certificate's own fields: `Subject` from the CN, `TenantID` from the first OU, and no roles. While the store was unavailable, an account the store would have refused (disabled, or with its binding withdrawn) came through as a certificate identity. Even with the store healthy, any certificate from a trusted client CA authenticated under a Subject and tenant its holder chose. With RBAC enabled the gate still denied such a role-less identity. With RBAC disabled, nothing else checks it, and handlers that scope per-user state on `(TenantID, Subject)`, such as the REST and MCP password vault, would serve the store of the user whose name matched the CN. The authenticator now refuses an unbound certificate with `auth.ErrCertNotBound`, recognized by qrdb's typed `UserNotFoundError`, and returns every other store error as `*auth.UserLookupError`. The certificate-field identity remains only for an authenticator built without a store, which is used when no qrdb identity plane is hosted. Behaviour change: on a qrdb-backed daemon, a trusted client certificate must be bound to a user to authenticate, even with `auth.enable_rbac: false`. On the ACME admin plane an unbound certificate is now answered 401 at authentication instead of 403 at the gate (go-xkms#1096).
- **The xkey IPC server now checks who is connecting, and `sudo xkey fido2` now resolves the same socket as the invoking user's desktop clients.** Before this change, `xkey/pkg/ipc/server.go` served every connection it accepted. The `0700` socket directory and `0600` socket file were its only access control, so any process that could reach the socket could ask for PKCS#11 signatures, stored passwords and autofill secrets. The server now checks every accepted connection before reading anything. It uses the same kernel peer-credential check (`verifyPeer`) and the same trusted set (`trustedUIDs`: this user, root, and the sudo user) as the client. `verifyPeer` now also returns the peer's uid. An untrusted client is closed without a response and logged at `Warn` with its `peer_uid`. On platforms where xkey reads no peer credentials (anything other than Linux, macOS and FreeBSD), the server drops every connection, the same way the client already refuses to connect (go-xkms#1137). Separately, sudo strips `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, so a daemon started with `sudo` fell back to `~/.xkey/run` while the invoking user's clients looked under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xkey/`, and the two never met. Under sudo (root with `SUDO_UID` set) and with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset, `runtimeDirFor` now picks `/run/user/$SUDO_UID` when that directory exists, is not a symlink, is owned by `SUDO_UID` and has mode `0700`. Otherwise it keeps the previous fallback (go-xkms#1138). **Behaviour change:** a client running as any user other than the server's user, root or the sudo user is now refused even if the socket's permissions would admit it.
- **Another local user could plant xkey's IPC socket and receive the victim's user PIN from `xkey unlock`. The socket directory is now checked on both ends, the client checks who is listening, and there is no shared `/tmp` fallback.** With `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset (typical on macOS and under cron, ssh or sudo), `xkey/pkg/ipc/socket.go` fell back to `/tmp/xkey-<uid>/xkey.sock`. `NewServer` accepted an existing directory at that path without checking its owner or mode, the GUI unlinked and took over a live socket, and every client dialed without checking the peer. Any user could create the directory first, listen in it, and collect PINs, passwords being saved by the browser extension, and PKCS#11 signing requests. Five changes close this. First, `runtimeDirFor` picks a per-user directory: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`; on macOS `$TMPDIR`, then `~/Library/Caches`; elsewhere `~/.xkey/run`. Under sudo it uses the invoking user's home. It never picks `/tmp`, and it yields no path, refused with `ErrSocketPathUnresolved`, when no home can be resolved. Second, `NewServer` creates each missing component with `Mkdir(0700)` and re-validates it straight away. It refuses (`ErrSocketDirInsecure`) a directory that is a symlink, is owned by anyone other than the user, root or the sudo user, or has any bit beyond `0700`, and it never chmods or chowns a directory it did not create (`xkey/pkg/ipc/socketdir.go`). Third, every IPC client goes through the new `ipc.Dial`, which validates the directory, connects, and then checks the listener's kernel-reported uid. That client set is `ipc.Client`, the PKCS#11 module transport (`xkey/pkg/pkcs11/ipc_transport.go`) and the native-messaging host (`xkey/pkg/nativemsg/host.go`). The uid comes from `SO_PEERCRED` on Linux and `LOCAL_PEERCRED` on macOS and FreeBSD. Other platforms fail closed with `ErrPeerCredentialsUnsupported`. Fourth, a stale socket is unlinked only if it is a socket owned by a trusted uid in a valid directory (`ipc.ReclaimSocket`). The GUI takes over a live socket only on `ErrSocketInUse`, and only through `ReclaimSocket`. A regular file at the socket path is never deleted. Fifth, handler failures no longer echo their wrapped detail to the client. The server logs the detail and the client receives `ipc: handler returned error`, or the bare sentinel for an invalid message, a sealed barrier or a disabled browser extension. Root and the sudo user are trusted because `sudo xkey fido2` runs as root on the invoking user's behalf. **Behaviour change:** a `--socket` directly under `/tmp` or any other shared or group-writable directory is now refused. Point `--socket` / `XKEY_IPC_SOCKET` at a `0700` directory you own (go-xkms#1117).

### Fixed

- **awskms `GetSymmetricKey` no longer treats a metadata-storage outage as "no seal key yet"** (#1119). It mapped every `storage.GetKey` failure to `backend.ErrKeyNotFound`, indistinguishable from a genuinely unprovisioned key. `seal.EnsureSealKey` (pkg/seal/cloud_provision.go) uses exactly that distinction to decide whether generating a replacement key is safe, so a storage outage during unseal could have driven it down the "provision a new key" path -- the mechanism #1098 found regenerating seal keys. Only `errors.Is(err, storage.ErrNotFound)` now maps to `ErrKeyNotFound`; every other error wraps `awskms.ErrMetadataStorage`, matching `getKeyID`'s existing classification (#839). The same collapse was also present in two other places, fixed the same way:
  - `awskms.Backend.ListKeys` silently dropped a key from its result on any per-key metadata read failure rather than just a genuine not-found race with `List`; it now surfaces the error instead of returning a misleadingly incomplete list.
  - `awskms.Backend.Get` (the FSEXT_PRIVATE_BLOB/FSEXT_PUBLIC_BLOB metadata path) reported every metadata-read failure as `backend.ErrFileNotFound`; only a genuine `storage.ErrNotFound` does now, everything else wraps `ErrMetadataStorage`. No caller in the tree currently branches on `errors.Is(err, backend.ErrFileNotFound)` from this path, so this closes the gap before anything comes to depend on the old, incorrect classification.
  - `vault.Backend.ListKeys` had the identical per-key collapse (falling back to a bare `{CN: cn}` entry on any metadata read failure, not just `storage.ErrNotFound`); it now returns `vault.ErrKeyRetrievalFailed` instead of silently truncating the list.
- **`CA.recordRevocation` now persists a revocation before it caches it, and checks for a duplicate through the replicated store, not only the in-memory map.** It used to insert into `ca.revocations` first and persist second: a failed store write still left the serial enforced on that node with no way to recover, because a retry hit the in-memory entry and returned `ErrAlreadyRevoked` for a record that had never actually been persisted. Its duplicate check also read only the map, so a node could revoke a serial another node already revoked and silently overwrite the original record's reason and time. The duplicate check now goes through `lookupRevocation` (the map, then the store), failing closed with a typed `ErrStorageError` on a store read fault; an existing record returns `ErrAlreadyRevoked` wrapped in `*errs.Detail` naming the original reason and time. The write itself uses `PutIfAbsent` -- `storage.Backend`'s unconditional create-if-absent primitive -- instead of a plain `Put`, and only a successful write updates the in-memory map (`cacheRevocation`) and triggers the CRL refresh that already followed it. A store write failure now returns a typed `*errs.Joined` wrapping `ErrStorageError` and the cause, with the map left untouched, so a retry after the store recovers persists instead of being rejected. For a replicated backend (every `go-qrdb`-backed `Backend` this package runs against), `PutIfAbsent` is a linearizable cross-node compare-and-swap keyed on "no record exists yet," so two nodes racing to revoke the same serial can both attempt the write but only one succeeds; the loser observes `stored=false` and reports `ErrAlreadyRevoked` with the winner's record read back through `lookupRevocation`, closing the race the duplicate check alone could not. Files: `pkg/ca/ca_extensions.go`, `pkg/ca/errors.go`. Verified by `pkg/ca/revocation_race_1131_test.go` (a failed `PutIfAbsent` leaves the map unchanged and a retry after recovery persists; two `*CA` instances over a shared store racing to revoke the same serial leave the loser with `ErrAlreadyRevoked` and the winner's reason/time intact; a store read fault during the duplicate check fails closed before any write is attempted), reusing the `pkg/ca/revocation_cluster_test.go` two-node harness. go-xkms#1131.
- **`xkey device`'s `--trust-new-devices` and `--timeout` (`device pair`/`device scan`) now actually read the config file and `XKEY_DEVICE_*` environment variables that were always documented as their sources, instead of silently ignoring them** (#1071). Both flags, plus `device pair --device`/`--force` and `device status --device`, were bound only with `viper.BindPFlag` against the package-level `viper` singleton `cmd/xkey/cmd` never calls `ReadInConfig`/`AutomaticEnv` on -- the binding made `viper.GetString`/`GetBool` on that key mirror the flag, but nothing ever called either, so a `device.trust_new_devices`/`device.scan_timeout` entry in `xkey.yaml` or an `XKEY_DEVICE_*` variable had no effect. `xkeyconfig.DeviceConfig` (`xkey/pkg/config/config.go`) is now the typed home for the two settings that have real config-file meaning -- `trust_new_devices` (default `false`) and `scan_timeout` (default `30s`, shared by `device pair`'s auto-discovery and `device scan`) -- resolved through the same flag-then-config-then-default precedence `device relay --listen` already used (`GetTrustNewDevices`, `resolveDeviceScanTimeout`, `cmd/xkey/cmd/device.go`), with a `Changed`-based flag check (`commandFlagChanged`, `cmd/xkey/cmd/xkmsd_client.go`) so an explicit `--trust-new-devices=false` still overrides a config file that turned the setting on. `device pair --device`/`--force` and `device status --device` have no config-file meaning -- they are per-invocation choices -- and now have no viper binding at all; they are read directly off the flag, as they already were in practice. Files: `xkey/pkg/config/config.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/device.go`, `device_pair.go`, `device_pair_stub.go`, `device_scan.go`, `xkmsd_client.go`. Verified by `xkey/pkg/config`'s `TestLoadFromPath_EnvOverride_DeviceSettings`, `TestLoadFromPath_DeviceSettings_FileBeatsDefault` and `TestValidate_*DeviceScanTimeout`, and `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/device_config_test.go`'s flag-beats-config-beats-default precedence tests and proof that the four per-invocation flags no longer mirror into viper.

## [0.35.0-alpha] - 2026-09-28

### Security

- **`pkg/backend/azurekv.Backend` now persists CN -> key metadata through `Config.KeyStorage` instead of an in-process map, so a restart no longer forces `pkg/seal.EnsureSealKey` to mint a new barrier seal key and orphan data sealed under the old one** (#1098, mirroring the `awskms` fix from #839). `Config.KeyStorage`/`CertStorage` were already required by `Config.Validate()`, but nothing in the package read or wrote through them: `CreateKey`, `CreateSecretKey`, `GenerateSymmetricKey`, `ImportKey`'s two branches, and the generic `Save` all wrote into an unexported `b.metadata map[string][]byte` that started empty every boot, and `Get`, `GetKey`, `GetSymmetricKey`, `ListKeys` and `Delete` read only that map. Every one of those paths now goes through `storage.SaveKey`/`GetKey`/`DeleteKey`/`KeyExists`/`ListKeys` against `b.config.KeyStorage`, exactly like `awskms.Backend`; `Backend.metadata` is removed. `Close` no longer clears `Config.KeyStorage` -- its lifecycle belongs to the caller, which may reuse it across a restart. The transient RSA wrapping-key material `GetImportParameters` generates for the import ceremony is unrelated key metadata (private key bytes, not a CN descriptor), so it now lives in a separate in-process-only `importTokens` map rather than being folded into the persisted store. A new `azurekv.ErrMetadataStorage` typed error joins the existing `ErrKeyRetrievalFailed`/`ErrKeyNotFound` for storage-layer failures. `gcpkms.Backend` was audited for the same gap and already persists every metadata write/read through `Config.KeyStorage`; no change was needed there.
  - Files: `pkg/backend/azurekv/{azurekv,azurekv_symmetric,azurekv_importexport,errors}.go`.
  - Verified by a new `TestBuildCloudKMSStrategy_AzureKVBackend_RestartReusesPersistedKey` in `pkg/seal/cloud_provision_azurekv_test.go` (mirroring the `awskms` restart test): a second `*azurekv.Backend` built over the same `Config.KeyStorage`/`CertStorage` and the same mock Key Vault resolves the first Backend's seal key through `GetSymmetricKey` without calling `SetSecret` again, and root-key material sealed before the restart unseals after it.
  - Also verified by new backend-level tests in `pkg/backend/azurekv/persistence_test.go`: metadata written by one `Backend` is visible to a second `Backend` over the same storage (and a delete on one is visible to the other), and a `storage.Backend` failure at each call site (`Exists`/`Put`/`Delete`/`List`/`Get`) surfaces as a typed error from `CreateKey`, `GenerateSymmetricKey`, `GetKey`, `Save`, `Delete`, `ListKeys` and `Get` rather than being silently swallowed.
- **FROST secret key shares are now actually protected at rest, on every whitelisted `backends.frost.secret_backend`** (#841). `pkg/keyprovider/frost.KeyStore` previously called `SecretBackend.GenerateKey`/`GetKey` with the share carried in `types.KeyAttributes.SealData` -- a field no backend (`software`, `pkcs8`, `tpm2`, `pkcs11`, `awskms`, `gcpkms`, `azurekv`, `vault`) ever implemented, so `StoreKeyPackage`/`LoadKeyPackage` either panicked or silently produced no secret at all. `KeyStore` now takes the secret backend as a `types.SealingKeyProvider` and seals the share with its native `types.Sealer` (TPM2 PCR-bound seal under the Platform SRK; PKCS#11/cloud KMS AES-256-GCM under a provisioned symmetric wrapping key; software/PKCS#8 HKDF-derived AES-GCM from a provisioned Ed25519 key), persisting the resulting opaque `types.SealedData` envelope alongside the group's public components instead of the share in the clear. `pkg/server`'s `ensureFrostSecretSealKey` provisions the wrapping key per `secret_backend` (via `seal.EnsureSealKey` for PKCS#11/cloud KMS, the new `seal.EnsurePrivateSealKey` for software/PKCS#8, nothing for TPM2), using a wrapping-key name distinct from the barrier's own (`xkms-frost-wrap` vs `xkms-barrier-seal`) so a backend serving both roles never shares one key between them. `cmd/xkmsctl`'s bespoke `fileSecretBackend`, which wrote every secret share to disk verbatim in the clear, is deleted; the CLI now seals through the same production software backend `xkmsd` uses. Files: `pkg/keyprovider/frost/{config.go,storage.go,wrapkey.go}`, `pkg/server/backend_frost.go`, `pkg/seal/cloud_provision.go`, `pkg/xkms/register_frost.go`, `cmd/xkmsctl/frost.go`, `sdk/go/{frost.go,seal.go}`. Verified by per-backend seal/unseal round-trip tests (software, PKCS#8, the TPM 2.0 simulator, SoftHSM2-backed PKCS#11, mocked AWS/GCP KMS, an in-process Vault Transit double), a restart-survival test, and typed-error tests for a wrong or missing wrapping key.
- **The gRPC transport no longer echoes internal error text to an
  unauthenticated or unauthorized caller.** `pkg/api/grpc/server.go`'s
  `authenticationUnaryInterceptor` and `authenticationStreamInterceptor`
  formatted `codes.Unauthenticated` with `"authentication failed: %v"`
  against the raw error `auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateGRPC` returned, so a
  user-store failure, a barrier failure, or the specific reason a
  certificate was rejected reached the client response. `pkg/api/grpc/service.go`'s
  `Service.authorize` — the single gate behind all 150+ RPC handlers — had
  the same defect on both its `codes.Unauthenticated` and
  `codes.PermissionDenied` paths, echoing the qrdb-backed authorizer's error
  text verbatim (`TestAuthz_AuthorizeDenied` asserted on the literal denial
  string, confirming the leak). Both interceptors now return the fixed
  `errAuthenticationFailed` ("authentication failed") message and log the
  cause server-side via the existing `s.logger.Warn`, already in place but
  previously logged in addition to, not instead of, leaking the same text to
  the client. `authorize` now returns the fixed `ErrAuthenticationRequired`
  ("grpc: authentication required") or `ErrAccessDenied`
  ("grpc: access denied") message and records the real reason in the audit
  event's `Details["reason"]`, so the cause stays in the audit trail rather
  than the client response — matching `pkg/api/rest/middleware.go`'s
  `AuthenticationMiddleware` and `pkg/api/rest/rbac_middleware.go`'s
  `RBACMiddleware`, which already followed this pattern. The QUIC transport
  serves the same `AuthenticationMiddleware` over HTTP/3 (`pkg/server/server.go`),
  so it was already unaffected; the ACME admin gRPC plane
  (`pkg/acme/api/server/interceptor_authz.go`) was already generic. Files:
  `pkg/api/grpc/{server,service,errors}.go`. Verified by new tests
  `TestAuthenticationUnaryInterceptor`/`TestAuthenticationStreamInterceptor`'s
  "does not leak internal error text to the client" subtests (a marker
  string in the authenticator's error is asserted absent from the gRPC
  status message and present in a captured `slog` logger), and updated
  `TestAuthz_AuthorizeDenied`/`TestAuthz_AuthorizeUnauthenticated`/
  `TestAuthz_GenerateKeyDenied`, which now assert the fixed message and that
  the denial reason lands in the audit event instead. go-xkms#1103.
- **Three authorization checks compared role names against the role IDs identities carry. Real Admin and SO users were refused, and a role name taken from an unverified token claim was honoured; all three now follow qrdb's authorization model.** Every store-resolved identity carries qrdb role identifiers in `Identity.Roles` (go-qrdb's middleware sets `Identity.Roles = user.RoleIDs`, and so does the mTLS authenticator since go-xkms#1069). Three sites called `identity.HasRole("admin"|"so"|"user"|"operator")`, so they never matched a real grant. They did match an identity whose roles were copied from an OIDC or JWT `roles`/`groups` claim for a subject with no qrdb user record.

  **Shared-password override** (`pkg/xkms/servicer_password.go`). This gates a non-owner updating or deleting a shared vault entry. Before the fix it failed closed for tenant Admins and SOs, who could not administer shared entries. It failed open for a name-bearing identity wherever the transport admitted one, which in practice means deployments with RBAC disabled. Admin and Operator hold identical `passwords:*` grants, so the override is a role-membership decision. It now uses the new `auth.HoldsSystemRole` (`pkg/auth/rolemembership.go`), which resolves the role's persisted identifier in the caller's own tenant through `qrdbsdk.ResolveSystemRoleID` and fails closed when no role client is wired or the store cannot answer.

  **CSR signing** (`pkg/xkms/servicer_ca.go`). Before the fix, REST `POST /api/v1/ca/sign-csr` and MCP `xkms.ca.sign-csr` refused every authenticated caller, the first-boot administrator included (fail-closed). The operation's declared permission is `certs:generate`, which every transport already enforces before dispatch. The servicer's second, name-based decision is removed, along with `xkms.ErrCSRSigningDenied`.

  **Tenant gate** (`pkg/api/tenantgate/tenantgate.go`). The Security Officer exemption never matched a real SO. It did let an identity claiming `so` skip the tenant-registered and tenant-sealed checks on REST, gRPC and MCP (fail-open). RBAC still applied afterwards. The exemption is removed: cross-tenant scope is qrdb's system-tenant rule alone (`auth.IsCrossTenant`). The system tenant's SO is unaffected, and a tenant-local officer is now scoped like any other tenant identity.

  `Identity.HasRole` is go-qrdb's and cannot be removed here, so a `forbidigo` rule in `.golangci.yml` now fails the lint gate on any call to it. `rest.RBACMiddleware.RequireRole`/`RequireAnyRole` made the same name comparison and had no callers; they are deleted.

  Tests run against a real in-memory qrdb node seeded by qrdb's own first-boot (`testutil.NewFirstBootNode`, which can also provision a tenant). At each site a seeded Admin or SO identifier is allowed, a lesser role is refused, and an identity carrying the role name gets nothing. See `pkg/auth/rolemembership_test.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_password_test.go`, `pkg/xkms/servicer_ca_test.go`, `pkg/api/mcp/authz_roleid_test.go` and `pkg/api/tenantgate/tenantgate_test.go`. The transport tests that asserted the SO exemption now assert its absence (go-xkms#1074).
- **device-attest-01's exported `VerifyQualifyingData` and its quote-era support code are removed; the substring-fallback weakness they carried had no caller and was not the live path.** #1060 asked for `VerifyQualifyingData` (`pkg/acme/challenges/device-attest-01/deviceattest01.go`, pre-change) to stop falling back to `bytes.Contains(certInfo, expectedData)` when its hand-rolled `ParseTPMSAttest` failed to parse `certInfo` -- the same substring-anywhere-in-the-structure weakness #789 (go-xkms#789/PR #1058) had already removed from the server's actual verification path, `verifyTPMEvidence` (`pkg/acme/challenges/device-attest-01/tpm.go:65`). Re-checking callers on top of #789 (root module, `sdk/go`, `xkey`, `test/integration`) confirmed `VerifyQualifyingData` had zero callers anywhere in the repo, including the client-side `Setup`/`SetupWithPCRs` evidence builders -- #789 had already routed `verifyTPMEvidence` through `pkg/attestation.VerifyInvariants` and `pkg/tpm2.VerifyCertify`, which compare TPMS_ATTEST `extraData` to the expected qualifying data with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` and no fallback (`pkg/tpm2/certify_verify.go:204-211`). `VerifyQualifyingData` was therefore not a second instance of the live bug to fix; it was dead code left behind by #789's rewrite, so this change removes it rather than strictifying it, per go-xkms's no-cruft policy. Removed with it, all confirmed to have zero callers repo-wide and to exist only in support of `VerifyQualifyingData`/each other: the hand-rolled `ParseTPMSAttest` (superseded by the canonical `tpm2.Unmarshal[tpm2.TPMSAttest]` decoder `pkg/tpm2/certify_verify.go:177` already uses), `ExtractPCRsFromCertInfo` (its own doc comment admitted it could not return real PCR values -- a PCR digest cannot be reversed into per-PCR contents -- so there was no design path to finish it as a half-built feature), the supporting types `TPMSAttest`/`TPMSClockInfo`/`TPMSQuoteInfo`/`TPMSPCRSelection`, and the `device-attest-01`-local sentinel `ErrPCRMismatch` (declared but never returned by any production code). `pkg/attestation.ErrPCRMismatch` and `pkg/acme/server/handlers.ErrPCRMismatch` are distinct, live symbols in other packages and are untouched. No second, strict qualifying-data implementation was added in this package: a caller that needs one goes through `pkg/attestation.VerifyInvariants`/`pkg/tpm2.VerifyCertify`, the existing canonical gate, rather than a second implementation living here. The `gotpm:"check"` struct tag on go-tpm's `TPMSAttest.Magic` is confirmed (by inspecting `go-tpm@v0.9.8/tpm2/reflect.go`) not to be wired to any unmarshal-time validation; the canonical gate already checks the TPM_GENERATED_VALUE magic explicitly rather than relying on the tag (`pkg/tpm2/certify_verify.go:181`), so no additional check was needed there. `ca.VerifyQuote` and the `nil`-PCRs gap noted in earlier drafts of this fix no longer exist on this base: #789 removed `VerifyQuote` from `AttestationVerifier` entirely along with the quote path it served. A separate, pre-existing gap -- `Setup`/`SetupWithPCRs` (`deviceattest01.go:510,631`) still build TPM2_Quote evidence via `TrustedPlatformModule.Quote`, which the TPM2_Certify-based `verifyTPMEvidence` now refuses -- was already identified in #789's own changelog entry (`security-device-attest-tpm-binding-789.md`) and is not addressed here. Docs: `docs/acme/challenges.md`'s device-attest-01 section, which still described the pre-#789 quote/PCR/`bytes.Contains`/`VerifyQuote` design, is corrected to describe the current TPM2_Certify flow, with the `Setup`/`SetupWithPCRs` gap called out explicitly. Verified by `pkg/acme/challenges/device-attest-01`'s existing test suite (unaffected: the removed functions' tests are deleted with them, nothing else referenced them) and `go test -race` across `pkg/acme/...` and `pkg/attestation/...`. go-xkms#1060, go-xkms#789.

### Added

- **`pkg/luks.Manager` now has `Mount`/`Unmount` methods, and its whole
  state machine rejects calls made out of order instead of silently
  proceeding** (#917). `Executor` gained `Mount(ctx, config)` and
  `Unmount(ctx, config)` — previously the interface had no mutating mount
  operation at all, only the `IsMounted` query, so nothing could ever set
  the `mounted` flag `Manager.IsMounted()` reads. `Manager.Mount` now
  returns `ErrNotUnlocked` if the volume isn't unlocked or `ErrAlreadyMounted`
  if it's already mounted, then sets `mounted` on a successful
  `Executor.Mount`; `Manager.Unmount` returns `ErrNotMounted` when not
  mounted, then clears it. `Manager.Unlock` now returns `ErrAlreadyUnlocked`
  on a second unlock, and `Manager.Lock` returns `ErrNotUnlocked` when the
  volume isn't unlocked — wiring up the four sentinel errors
  (`ErrNotMounted`, `ErrAlreadyMounted`, `ErrNotUnlocked`,
  `ErrAlreadyUnlocked`) that were declared in `pkg/luks/errors.go` but never
  returned by anything. Files: `pkg/luks/manager.go`, `pkg/luks/manager_test.go`;
  re-exported unchanged by `sdk/go/luks` (type aliases, no source changes
  needed there). Verified by new success/error/state-guard tests for
  `Mount`/`Unmount` and the four sentinels, `GOWORK=off go test -race
  ./pkg/luks/... ./sdk/go/luks/...`.

  A production `Executor` backed by `github.com/jeremyhahn/go-luks2` (the
  pure-Go LUKS2 library already used by this repository's `xkey` module,
  `xkey/go.mod`) is **not** included in this change: it is a new dependency
  for the root `go-xkms` module and is being held for explicit owner
  approval before it lands, still tracked under #917. `pkg/luks.Executor`
  therefore still has no production implementation in this repository —
  only `mockExecutor` in tests.

### Changed

- **ACME admin authorization denials are now logged server-side with their cause on every admin transport.** `PermissionGate.Authorize` (`pkg/acme/admin/authz.go`) — the one seam REST (`Wrap`), gRPC (`UnaryAuthorizationInterceptor`) and MCP (`authorizeMCPMethod`) all call to reach the qrdb RBAC decision — now takes the caller's transport context (HTTP method/path, gRPC full method, or MCP JSON-RPC method name) and logs it at `Warn` alongside the identity's subject and tenant, the requested resource:action, and the authorizer's error, on every denial and on the unauthenticated path. Previously only an unmapped operation was logged; a denial with a valid mapping left no server-side trail of who was refused, for what, or why. The fix is entirely server-side: REST still answers the fixed "Access denied: insufficient permissions" detail, gRPC the fixed `PermissionDenied` message, and MCP its fixed JSON-RPC error code — none of them gain the cause text (go-xkms#1110).
- **`pkg/backend/azurekv`'s symmetric-key path now goes through an
  injectable `SecretsClient` seam instead of constructing a real
  `*azsecrets.Client` inline, so `GenerateSymmetricKey`/`GetSymmetricKey`
  are unit-testable without live Azure credentials.** Standard-tier Key
  Vault has no oct (symmetric) key type through the Keys API, so these two
  methods (`azurekv_symmetric.go`) generate AES key material locally and
  persist it as a Key Vault secret; `storeSymmetricKeySecret`/
  `retrieveSymmetricKeySecret` previously built their own
  `azidentity`/`azsecrets.NewClient` credential chain on every call, with no
  way to substitute a test double, mirroring the exact gap `KeyVaultClient`
  already closed for the Keys API side of this backend. `SecretsClient`
  lists the two `azsecrets.Client` operations that path calls
  (`SetSecret`/`GetSecret`); `*azsecrets.Client` already satisfies it
  directly, so no wrapper type is needed. `initSecretsClient` mirrors
  `initClient`'s double-checked-locking lazy init, and the new
  `NewBackendWithClients(config, keyClient, secretsClient)` constructor
  injects both clients for tests, alongside the existing
  `NewBackendWithClient` (keys client only). `MockSecretsClient`
  (`mock_client.go`, exported like the existing `MockKeyVaultClient` so it
  is reusable across package boundaries) is an in-memory fake supporting
  injected `SetSecret`/`GetSecret` errors, direct value overrides for
  malformed-data cases, and a call counter. Verified by new tests in
  `pkg/backend/azurekv/azurekv_symmetric_test.go` (happy-path round trip,
  `SetSecret`/`GetSecret` failures, a secret deleted out of band from Key
  Vault, and malformed secret data — a nil value and non-base64 content) and
  by `pkg/seal/cloud_provision_azurekv_test.go`, which proves
  `seal.BuildCloudKMSStrategy`/`EnsureSealKey` provision and reuse the
  barrier's seal key through the real `azurekv.Backend` and complete a
  genuine `SealRootKey`/`UnsealRootKey` round trip, the same proof
  `cloud_provision_awskms_test.go` already gives for AWS KMS. Coverage of
  `azurekv_symmetric.go` rises from 40.9% to 70.1% (package total 77.1% to
  83.2%). go-xkms#1090.

### Removed

- **BREAKING: `password get` no longer accepts `decrypt`/`user_pin`.** Every
  store reachable through `XKMSService.PasswordGet`
  (`staticpw.BackendStore`, `staticpw.ScopedStore`, `staticpw.DAOStore`)
  returns an entry exactly as stored; confidentiality at rest is the tenant
  barrier's, not a per-request decryption step, so the fields could never be
  honoured and were previously rejected with `ErrPasswordDecryptNotSupported`
  whenever either was set. Removed end to end instead of being kept as
  accepted-but-rejected fields: `xkmsctl password get`'s `--decrypt` and
  `--user-pin` flags (`cmd/xkmsctl/password.go`), the `Decrypt`/`UserPIN`
  fields on `transport.PasswordGetRequest` (`pkg/api/transport/types.go`) and
  every transport that populated them (gRPC, Unix, QUIC), the gRPC
  `PasswordGetRequest.decrypt` proto field — number `2` and the name
  `decrypt` are now `reserved` in `xkmsv1.PasswordGetRequest`
  (`pkg/api/grpc/proto/xkmsv1/xkms.proto`) and regenerated with the pinned
  `protoc`/`protoc-gen-go`/`protoc-gen-go-grpc` toolchain — and the
  now-unreachable `xkms.ErrPasswordDecryptNotSupported` sentinel. `password
  get` on an unlocked session still returns the entry, including the
  password field, unchanged; a locked session still fails with
  `staticpw.ErrStoreLocked`. Docs updated to match
  (`docs/password-vault/{cli,api,user,engineering}.md`), including
  correcting `engineering.md`'s references to a `migration.go` and an
  `encrypted_store.go` that do not exist in `pkg/staticpw`, and the
  `pkg/staticpw` package comment's reference to a nonexistent
  `types.SymmetricEncrypter` interface. go-xkms#1061.

### Fixed

- **`ChallengeServer` exposes the bound listener address, removing a reserve-close-rebind port race in its own test suite** (#1104). `challenge_test.go`'s `freePort` helper asked the kernel for a port on `:0`, closed the listener, and returned the number for `ChallengeServer.Start` to rebind moments later; any other process on the host, including another package's test binary running in parallel, could take the same ephemeral port in that window, which is what failed CI with `bind: address already in use` on `TestChallengeServer_HandleChallenge_Success`. `ChallengeServer` now records the `net.Listener` `Start` binds and exposes it through a new `Addr() net.Addr` method, so a caller that starts the server with port `"0"` reads back the kernel-assigned port after a successful bind instead of pre-allocating and releasing one. `Start`'s bind behavior, including the port callers configure in production (`SetupHTTP01Challenge`, defaulting to `80`), is unchanged. The test suite now starts servers on port `"0"` and reads `Addr()`, eliminating the race for every test that runs its own server; the two tests that intentionally occupy a port to assert `Start` fails (`TestChallengeServer_Start_PortInUse`, `TestSetupHTTP01Challenge_PortInUse`) now hold that listener open for the life of the test instead of releasing it first. Files: `pkg/acme/client/service/challenge.go`, `pkg/acme/client/service/challenge_test.go`. Verified with `go test -race -count=20 ... -run ChallengeServer`.
- **The REST transport requests collection roots at exactly the paths xkmsd registers** (#1087). `PasswordAdd`/`PasswordList`, `CreateCustodianGroup`/`ListCustodianGroups`, `ListShares` and `QueryAudit` requested their collection root without the trailing slash that `pkg/api/rest/routes.go` registers. chi's slash redirect hid the mismatch until another module claimed the bare path, which is how #949 found the tenant case. A parity test now derives each collection-root pattern from `pkg/api/rest.Routes()` and checks the transport against an exact-match server with no redirect.
- **`xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd` builds and vets again without the `ble` tag** (#1081). `dial_xkmsd_test.go` referenced `XKMSdBridgeConfig`/`dialXKMSd` with no build constraint of its own, but those symbols lived only in `fido2_phone_bridge.go`, which carries `//go:build ble` for the phone-pairing bridge it also defines -- so `GOWORK=off go vet ./...` (no tags, CI's default) failed with `undefined: XKMSdBridgeConfig`. `dialXKMSd`, `createXKMSdClient`, `XKMSdBridgeConfig` and their defaults/errors have no BLE dependency of their own; they moved into a new untagged `dial_xkmsd.go` so `dial_xkmsd_test.go` can stay untagged and exercise the xkmsd dial path directly. `fido2_phone_bridge.go` keeps `//go:build ble` and now holds only the BLE-specific phone-bridge wiring (`phoneBackendWithBridge`, `connectXKMSdBridge`, `ErrXKMSdBridgeCreationFailed`). Files: `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/dial_xkmsd.go` (new), `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/fido2_phone_bridge.go`. Verified by `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags ble ./...`, and `go vet -tags "ble codec_json tpm_simulator" ./...` all passing clean from `xkey/`, and `go test -race -tags "ble codec_json tpm_simulator" ./cmd/xkey/cmd/...` passing.
- **`xkmsctl tenant create`/`list` reach the crypto-plane tenant service again** (#949). The REST transport requested `/api/v1/tenants` without the trailing slash, while xkmsd registers the collection root as `/api/v1/tenants/`. chi's slash redirect used to bridge the gap, until the ACME admin plane claimed the exact bare path for its own tenant surface. From then on those calls silently got the admin handler's differently-shaped body and decoded to an empty `TenantInfo`, with no error. `pkg/api/transport/rest` now requests the trailing-slash path; regression tests place a decoy handler at the bare path.

## [0.34.0-alpha] - 2026-09-28

### Security

- **Every ACME admin route on xkmsd's unified mTLS listener answered 403, even to the first-boot administrator; mTLS callers now reach qrdb RBAC as their bound qrdb user with that user's role IDs.** Two defects in the chain from client certificate to authorization decision caused it. First, `cmd/xkmsd/admin.go` `finalizeAdminModule` built the admin plane's mTLS authenticator with no user store, so it could only read certificate fields: the identity reaching `PermissionGate` carried no roles and no tenant, and go-qrdb's authorizer, which unions the grants of `Identity.Roles`, denied every `gate.Wrap` permission. The authenticator is now built with `auth.QRDBUserStore`, as the crypto plane's is. Second, `pkg/auth/qrdb_userstore.go` reported only the user's first role, translated to its name, while go-qrdb looks roles up by ID. Wiring the store alone therefore still failed with `role: not found: admin`, and the same failure hit every mTLS identity that `pkg/server` and the REST host resolved through that store. `auth.MTLSUser.Role string` is now `Roles []string` and carries every qrdb role ID verbatim, which is go-qrdb's own identity contract (its middleware sets `Identity.Roles = user.RoleIDs`). `NewQRDBUserStore` no longer takes a role client. The admin plane declares no permissions of its own: every one it demands is already registered by qrdb and granted to the built-in roles, so none is registered by xkms. `cmd/xkmsd/admin_authz_test.go` walks the published admin router against a first-boot-seeded embedded node. It shows that the first-boot administrator passes the gate on every route, that a roleless user and a certificate bound to no user are refused on every route, and that every permission the routes demand is registered with qrdb and held by the seeded Owner role (go-xkms#1069).

### Added

- **An operator can point the `aws_kms` barrier seal key at an existing AWS KMS CMK instead of letting xkmsd/xkey provision one** (#842). `backends.awskms.key_id` (xkmsd) and `barrier.cloud_kms.aws_kms.key_id` / `xkey barrier init --aws-key-id` (xkey) accept a key ID, key ARN, alias, or alias ARN, threaded into `awskms.Config.KeyID` at every construction site (`pkg/server/backend_awskms.go`, `pkg/server/platform_store_awskms.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/barrier_cloudkms_awskms.go`). `awskms.Config.Validate` rejects a malformed value with the typed `ErrInvalidKeyID`, matching AWS's own key-ID/ARN/alias/alias-ARN shapes (including multi-Region `mrk-` keys and the `aws-cn`/`aws-us-gov` partitions). `pkg/seal.EnsureSealKey` now fails closed with a new typed `ErrOperatorSealKeyNotFound` when an operator-configured key resolves not-found at barrier init, instead of silently falling through to `GenerateSymmetricKey` and provisioning a different, unrequested CMK. Existence is still checked against the live AWS KMS API the first time the key is resolved (`DescribeKey`). Files: `pkg/backend/awskms/config.go`, `pkg/seal/cloud_provision.go`, `pkg/config/config.go`, `xkey/pkg/config/barrier_cloud.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/barrier_cloudkms{,_awskms}.go`. Verified by `pkg/backend/awskms/config_test.go` (every accepted key-ID/ARN/alias/alias-ARN shape, and malformed-value rejection), `pkg/seal/cloud_provision_test.go` and `cloud_provision_awskms_test.go` (an operator-configured key is resolved and reused with `CreateKey` never called; a missing operator key fails closed with `ErrOperatorSealKeyNotFound` and never calls `CreateKey`; the no-`key_id` create path is unchanged), and `xkey/pkg/config/barrier_cloud_test.go` (`KeyID` round-trips through `Save`/`Load`).

### Fixed

- **The ACME admin gRPC permission map is keyed by the real method names, and covers the account operations** (#743). `MethodPermissions` (`pkg/acme/api/server/interceptor_authz.go`) used hand-written `"/admin.v1.AdminService/..."` keys. The generated service is `trustedca.admin.v1.AdminService`, so every call would have missed the map and been denied as unmapped once the server is wired. The map is now keyed by the generated `adminv1.AdminService_*_FullMethodName` constants. It also gains `ListAccounts`, `GetAccount` and `DisableAccount`, with the same permissions REST and MCP already enforce. A test checks the map against the service descriptor in both directions.
- **BREAKING: ACME certificates are now keyed by their full X.509 serial
  number, not its low 64 bits.** `OrderFinalizeHandler` stored an issued
  certificate's `ACMECertificate.ID` (and the "id" segment of its
  `/acme/cert/{id}` URL) as `cert.SerialNumber.Uint64()`, silently taking the
  low 64 bits of the CA's 128-bit serial (`pkg/ca.SerialNumberBits`) when it
  overflowed `uint64` - so two certificates whose serials happened to share
  those bits collided in storage, and the second issuance silently
  overwrote the first's record. `entities.ACMECertificate.Serial` now holds
  the certificate's complete serial number as a canonical lowercase hex
  string (no truncation, no precision loss), and it is what
  `/acme/cert/{id}` and certificate revocation key on; the DAO's own numeric
  row key is an FNV-1a hash of `Serial` (`entities.StringToEntityID`,
  mirroring `Tenant` and `ExternalAccountBinding`), kept only to satisfy the
  generic DAO's `uint64` entity-ID contract, and is never a certificate's
  public identity. `/acme/cert/{id}` accepts an optional `0x`/`0X` prefix and
  normalizes case, so differently-spelled encodings of the same serial reach
  the same record; a malformed or non-positive serial in the URL is rejected
  with a typed `*entities.InvalidSerialError` (surfaced as an ACME
  `malformed` error), never a panic. `pkg/acme/admin`'s certificate lookups
  already matched on the full decimal serial parsed from the stored PEM and
  are unaffected. No migration is provided (pre-release alpha): existing
  stored `ACMECertificate` records keyed by the old truncated numeric ID are
  no longer reachable by that ID and must be re-issued if still needed.
  Follow-up: the new FNV-1a row key is itself only 64 bits, so a hash
  collision between two DIFFERENT full serials remains possible in
  principle (astronomically unlikely, but the whole point of this fix).
  Certificate fetch (`CertificateHandler`) and revoke (`RevokeCertHandler`)
  now verify the fetched row's `Serial` matches the requested serial and
  treat a mismatch as not-found, never serving or revoking the wrong
  certificate. `storage.SaveCertificateNoCollision` (used by
  `OrderFinalizeHandler` and the ACME client's local certificate cache)
  refuses to overwrite a row already holding a different certificate,
  returning a typed `*storage.CertificateSerialCollisionError`; it uses the
  DAO's atomic `SaveIfAbsent` when the backing store supports it, and falls
  back to a Get-then-Save sequence otherwise (not atomic against a
  concurrent writer - go-qrdb does not expose a way through the SDK
  boundary to detect "atomic unsupported" as distinct from other
  `SaveIfAbsent` failures, so this function cannot do better without a new
  go-qrdb primitive, which it does not add). `admin.CertificateInfo.ID` and
  its SDK mirror are removed - no consumer read it, and it was an opaque
  internal storage hash with no business being on the wire; `SerialNumber`
  is the certificate's identity. (go-xkms#744).
- **`server.New` now runs `config.Validate` itself, instead of trusting the caller to have already — BREAKING for an embedder that constructs `*config.Config` by hand.** `config.Load` always called `Validate`, but `New` did not, so a hand-built configuration (an embedder, or a test) could reach subsystem init with a shape `Load` would have refused. The sharpest case: an empty `storage.path` reached `initializePINManager`, which built its state directory by string concatenation (`Storage.Path + "/pin"`), resolving to the filesystem root's own `/pin` directory. `New` now calls `cfg.Validate()` first, before touching the filesystem or storage at all, and wraps a failure in `*ErrServiceInit{Service: "configuration"}`; `Validate` also normalizes `cfg` in place (defaults `Storage.Backend` to `"pebble"`, `Storage.QRDB.Transport` to `"embedded"`, `Cluster.ShardID` to `1`), so every subsystem `New` initializes afterward sees the normalized values. `initializePINManager` (`pkg/server/server.go`) additionally builds its path with `filepath.Join` and guards an empty `storage.path` with a typed `*ErrConfigRequired`, for defense in depth if it is ever reached without going through `New` (its PIN store is always file-backed, independent of `storage.backend`). `initializePasswordStore` also switches to `filepath.Join`; it has no equivalent hard guard because its real write already goes through the backend-aware `createStorage` seam, which never touches `storage.path` for a `qrdb` backend. The loopback desktop engine (`pkg/server/loopback`) forces `Protocols.REST` on for its 127.0.0.1-only listener, which makes `Validate`'s network-serving check (`storage.backend "qrdb"` + `tls.enabled`) trip on a launch that never leaves the loopback interface; it now sets the new `config.Config.LoopbackDesktop` field (`yaml:"-"`, unreachable from any config file/env/flag) and `Validate` honours it to skip exactly that requirement, nothing else. Files: `pkg/server/server.go`, `pkg/config/config.go`, `pkg/server/loopback/loopback.go`. An embedder that was relying on `New` accepting a configuration `config.Load` would have refused must fix the configuration; there is no compatibility shim. Verified by `TestNew_EmptyStoragePath_RejectedBeforeAnyFilesystemWrite` (nothing is created under the working directory), `TestNew_InvalidConfig_RejectedWithTypedError`, `TestNew_ValidConfig_Succeeds`, `TestConfig_Validate_LoopbackDesktopExemptsNetworkServingRequirements`, `TestConfig_Validate_LoopbackDesktopDoesNotExemptOtherRESTConfigs`, and the existing `pkg/server/loopback` suite (a real loopback launch still succeeds). Making `New` always validate also exposed a `backends.tpm2` validation defect that would otherwise have been a startup regression for every `use_simulator: true` deployment (including `test/integration/api/config.test.yaml`, which sets no `device_path`): `Validate` required `device_path` even when `use_simulator` is true, though the simulator is addressed by `simulator_host`/`simulator_port` and never opens `device_path` at all. `Validate` now requires `device_path` only when `use_simulator` is false; verified by `TestValidate_Backends/TPM2_simulator_without_device_path` (accepted) alongside the existing `TestValidate_Backends/TPM2_enabled_without_device_path_(hardware)` (still refused with the same typed error). go-xkms#666.
- **`xkey piv`, `xkey fido2` and `xkey device listen`/`sync*` now honour the
  config file and environment variable sources they advertised (or should
  have), instead of silently reading only their command-line flag —
  BREAKING for `--pkcs11-pin`/`--pkcs11-so-pin`.** The global `viper`
  instance these commands bound flags to (`root.go:245-247`'s own comment
  called it "phased out") was never pointed at a config file and never had
  `AutomaticEnv` enabled, so every `piv.*`/`device.listen.*`/`device.sync*.*`
  key it exposed only ever reflected the bound flag's current value; the
  `fido2` command's Long help claimed `XKEY_FIDO2_*`/config-file support for
  every flag when only `fido2.attestation` was actually wired, and even that
  wiring was itself blind to `pkg/config`'s own `fido2.storage`/
  `storage_path`/`device_name` keys. `xkeyconfig.PIVConfig`
  (`pkg/config/config.go:93-107`) is new: `--backend`, `--piv-storage`,
  `--storage-path`, `--tpm-device`, `--pkcs11-library` and `--pkcs11-token`
  now resolve flag-then-config/environment-then-backend-matched-default
  through it, the same precedence `resolveXKMSdURL` already used for the
  xkmsd endpoint; `buildPIVConfig` (`cmd/xkey/cmd/piv.go:603-639`) and every
  command that builds PIV storage (`piv`, `cert request`/`show`/`export`,
  `device listen`, `provision`, `auth login --piv`) go through it. The
  PKCS#11 PIN and Security Officer PIN deliberately stay out of that config
  section and out of any generic environment binding: `--pkcs11-pin` and
  `--pkcs11-so-pin` value flags are gone (a value on the command line is
  visible to every other process on the host via `ps`, the same reason
  `--pin`/`--so-pin` were removed in #272) and are replaced by
  `--pkcs11-pin-stdin`/`XKEY_PIV_PKCS11_PIN` and
  `--pkcs11-so-pin-stdin`/`XKEY_PIV_PKCS11_SO_PIN`
  (`pivPKCS11PINSource`/`pivPKCS11SOPINSource`, `piv.go:57-69`), the same
  stdin-then-dedicated-env-var convention `pin_input.go` already used for the
  host PIN service's own PIN. `buildFIDO2Config`
  (`cmd/xkey/cmd/fido2.go:553-596`) now installs `fido2.storage`,
  `fido2.storage_path` and `fido2.device_name` from the loaded config the
  same way it already did for `fido2.attestation`, and the command's Long
  help now names exactly the four flags (`--storage`, `--storage-path`,
  `--name`, `--attestation`) that have a config/environment source instead of
  claiming all of them do. `device listen`'s and `device sync`/`sync-push`/
  `sync-pull`/`sync-status`'s `viper.BindPFlag` calls were dead code — bound
  but never read back through `viper.Get*` anywhere, since both commands
  already read their flags directly off `cmd.Flags()` — and are deleted
  rather than wired up: `sync`'s `--trust-store`/`--oath`/`--passwords`/
  `--all`/`--dry-run` select what one invocation does and have no config-file
  meaning, and `listen`'s `--help` never claimed a config/environment source
  to begin with. Files: `pkg/config/config.go`, `pkg/config/load_test.go`,
  `pkg/config/config_test.go`, `cmd/xkey/cmd/piv.go`, `pin_input.go`,
  `auth_piv.go`, `cert.go`, `piv_import.go`, `piv_generate.go`, `piv_csr.go`,
  `provision.go`, `device_listen.go`, `device_sync.go`, `fido2.go`, and the
  corresponding `_test.go` files; docs:
  `xkey/docs/piv/{cli,engineering,architecture}.md`,
  `xkey/docs/virtual-authenticator/cli.md`, `xkey/docs/fido2/README.md`,
  `xkey/docs/device/engineering.md` (go-xkms#871).

## [0.33.0-alpha] - 2026-09-28

### Security

- **device-attest-01's `tpm` format now binds the attested key to the CSR key, and verifies the evidence as the WebAuthn TPM2_Certify it is instead of as a quote** (#789). Before this change, any genuine device's attestation authorized a certificate for any key. The verifier called `VerifyQuote` and then looked for the key authorization anywhere in `certInfo` with `bytes.Contains`, never parsed the `TPMS_ATTEST`, and never read `pubArea`. `verifyTPMEvidence` now applies WebAuthn Level 2 §8.3, with no change to the wire format:
  - `certInfo` must carry `TPM_GENERATED_VALUE` and be `TPM_ST_ATTEST_CERTIFY`, and its attested Name must be Name(`pubArea`).
  - `extraData` must equal `TPMExtraData(alg, keyAuthorization)`, which is `alg`'s hash of the key authorization.
  - `sig` must verify under `x5c[0]` with `alg`.
  - `x5c[0]` must meet §8.3.1: version 3, an empty subject, a TCG SAN, not a CA, and EKU `tcg-kp-AIKCertificate`.

  Every `x5c` entry must be a certificate before the chain is anchored. `bindsThroughTheCSR` now covers `tpm`, so `Verify` refuses it with `ErrKeyBindingRequired`. `BindCSRKey` gains a TPM arm that checks the CSR self-signature, re-verifies the recorded certification, and requires `pubArea`'s key to equal the CSR's key. There is still one binding gate. `attestation.Evidence` gains `AttesterCertificate` and `CertifySignatureAlgorithm`. The TPM2 profile reads its challenge from the certification's `extraData` and compares the certified key with `SubjectSPKI` when that is set. `pkg/tpm2.VerifyCertifyByCertificate` verifies a certification whose attester is an X.509 AIK. `AttestationVerifier.VerifyQuote` and `ErrQuoteVerificationFailed` are removed, and `ErrTPMAttestationInvalid` and `ErrAIKCertificateInvalid` are added.
  - Files: `pkg/acme/challenges/device-attest-01/{tpm,binding,deviceattest01}.go`, `pkg/attestation/invariants.go`, `pkg/tpm2/certify_verify.go`.
  - Verified by `tpm_simulator_test.go`. It uses real TPM2_Certify and TPM2_Quote output from the in-process simulator and accepts the device's own key. It refuses a software key, a quote, another `pubArea`, the challenge outside `extraData`, a wrong `extraData`, a second AIK's signature, and an unanchored `x5c`.
  - Also verified by `pkg/attestation/invariants_tpm_test.go` and `pkg/tpm2/certify_verify_certificate_test.go`.
  - The challenge is not yet wired into xkmsd (#737/#828), so no deployment changes behaviour.
  - The client half (`Setup`, `pkg/acme/client` `setupAttestChallenge`) still emits quote evidence, which this verifier refuses.

### Fixed

- **The unified API server's client-CA pool now keeps the operator's configured `tls.ca_file`/`tls.client_cas` after the embedded CA composes, instead of silently dropping them** (#794 triage). `upgradeUnifiedTLSCert` used to replace `tls.Config`'s client-CA pool outright with the CA bundle (`ca.CATrustPools.CABundleCertPool()`), so an mTLS client anchored only by an operator-configured client CA stopped being accepted the moment the CA composed, even though `tls.client_cas` still named that CA. It now installs the union of the configured client CAs -- resolved through the same `loadClientCAsUnion` helper `buildTLSConfig` uses at startup, via the new `unifiedClientCAPool` -- and the CA's bundle, so both continue to verify. A re-read `tls.client_cas` failure surfaces as the existing typed `*ErrCertParse`/`*ErrFileRead` rather than being swallowed; a CA-bundle fetch failure degrades only the pool (typed `*ErrTLSCertOp`, logged) while the certificate upgrade still proceeds. Files: `pkg/server/unified_tls.go`. Verified by `pkg/server/unified_client_ca_pool_test.go` and `pkg/server/unified_tls_test.go`.
- **The Platform SRK's shape now agrees between the simulator first-boot backend autodetect and the operator enrollment ceremony** (#997). `pkg/backend/tpm2/config.go`'s `ToTPMConfig` hardcoded `PlatformPolicy: false` into the `PlatformSRKConfig` it built, so a Platform SRK created by `provisionSimulatorEKSRK`'s first-boot recipe carried no PCR-policy `AuthPolicy` in its template at all -- disagreeing with the always-`PlatformPolicy: true` PSRK `pkg/tpm2`'s enrollment path (`PlatformKeyStore.Initialize`/`EnrollPlatformSRK`, and `DefaultConfig`) has created since #677 settled the design (`authValue` = user PIN, `authPolicy` = platform PCR policy). `pkg/server/platform_store.go`'s `buildTPM2PlatformSealer` papered over the mismatch by forcing the `KeyAttributes` it returned to `PlatformPolicy: true` regardless of what the TPM object actually was, so a Platform SRK backend-probed on a fresh simulator authorized through the wrong compound-policy branch and every `Seal`/`Unseal` against it failed.
  - `ToTPMConfig` now always sets `PlatformSRK.PlatformPolicy: true`, matching `pkg/tpm2.DefaultConfig`; there is no plain-password shape for the Platform SRK to fall back to.
  - `buildTPM2PlatformSealer` no longer overrides `PlatformSRKAttributes()`'s resolved `PlatformPolicy` -- it already derives correctly from configuration (`pkg/tpm2/key.go`'s `PlatformSRKAttributesFromConfig`), and forcing it masked exactly this kind of shape mismatch instead of surfacing it.
  - `CreateSRK` needed no change: it already derives the AuthPolicy baked into a Platform SRK's template from the live platform PCR at creation time (`capturePlatformPolicyPin`), independent of whether `CreatePlatformPolicy` has run -- both the simulator autodetect path and the enrollment path already relied on this and never called `CreatePlatformPolicy` first, so making both agree on `PlatformPolicy: true` is sufficient for them to derive identical `AuthPolicy` digests from the same PCR state.
  - Verified with a new `pkg/backend/tpm2` test that provisions a Platform SRK through each path independently and asserts their persisted `AuthPolicy` digests match, a PIN-branch round trip proving key operations under an enrolled Platform SRK still work, and a `pkg/server` fresh-probe Seal/Unseal round trip through `buildTPM2PlatformSealer` -- the path this bug actually broke and that no existing test exercised end to end.

## [0.32.0-alpha] - 2026-09-27

### Added

- **A public-releasability gate: `make check-public-literals` fails on lab addresses, fleet host names or owner paths in the tree, and CI's lint job runs it** (#1030). The patterns are written in exactly one place, the header of `scripts/check-public-literals.sh`, the only file allowed to contain them apart from the agent-instruction files. The existing occurrences are scrubbed. Docs and fixtures now use RFC 5737 addresses, `example.com` hosts and repository-relative or `$HOME` paths. The ACME integration compose file mounts its sibling repositories by relative path, as it already did for its other siblings. Verified by `test/scripts/check-public-literals.test.sh` (a planted literal fails the gate, and a clean tree passes).
- **Several xkey instances can run side by side under one UID, one per agent, each with its own socket and its own paired Chrome profile** (#1033). The IPC socket now derives from `XKEY_HOME` when it is set (`<XKEY_HOME>/run/xkey.sock`, or a hashed runtime-dir path when that would exceed the `sun_path` limit). `--socket` is now one persistent root flag bound to `XKEY_IPC_SOCKET` and honoured by every command, replacing the per-command copies on `fido2`, `extension serve` and `extension host`. The `fido2` daemon listens exactly where its clients resolve. The `fido2.socket` config key is removed: use `--socket` or `XKEY_IPC_SOCKET`. `xkey extension install|uninstall chrome --profile-dir <dir>` writes a per-profile native-messaging manifest whose launcher pins `XKEY_HOME`. Files: `xkey/pkg/ipc/socket.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/{root,state_source,extension,fido2}.go` and the commands that took `--socket`, `xkey/pkg/nativemsg/manifest.go`; `SKILL.md` documents running as one of several instances. Verified by `instance_isolation_test.go` (two daemons under one UID; a client naming B never sees A's credential), `extension_profile_dir_test.go` and `profile_manifest_test.go`.
- **`xkey provision --agent <name>` sets up a complete xkey instance for an agent in one unattended step** (#1033). In one command it:
  - generates the agent's SSH service key;
  - initializes the barrier;
  - sets the host PIN service's SO and user PINs;
  - initializes the FIDO2 token (with persistent storage);
  - generates the four primary PIV slots;
  - records the display name in the instance's own `config.yaml`;
  - optionally pairs a Chrome profile (`--chrome-profile-dir`).

  The target home must be named with `--home` or `XKEY_HOME`, never the operator's default home, and an initialized home is refused without `--force`. The command takes three distinct secrets through xkey's existing inputs: the user PIN (`--pin-stdin`/`XKEY_PIN`), the SO PIN (`--so-pin-stdin`/`XKEY_SO_PIN`) and the barrier password (`--barrier-password[-file]`/`XKEY_BARRIER_PASSWORD`). A missing one is refused by name, and no secret stands in for another. It prints human-readable output or `--json` with no secrets. Verified by `provision_test.go`, including a four-way check that the SO PIN verifies only as SO and the user PIN only as user.

### Fixed

- **The phone bridge's OATH, PIV and sync methods now do real work, instead of reporting success and doing nothing** (#690). Of the 13 `remote.*` bridge handlers that were placeholders:
  - `remote.oathAdd`/`oathGenerate` now use the configured `oath.Store` and generator;
  - `remote.pivListSlots`/`pivGetCert` use the per-backend `xkms.PIVCertificateStorage`;
  - `remote.pivSign` signs with the slot's key through the ordinary key backend;
  - the five `remote.sync*` methods use `sync.Service`: union-merge for the trust store, last-modified-wins for OATH and passwords.

  `xkey device listen` wires these to the same stores `xkey oath`, `xkey piv` and `xkey device sync` use (`buildListenBridgeConfig`). A handler without its service now answers `ErrorCodeFeatureUnavailable` (-32035). The three `remote.*Backup` methods now return that error too, instead of a fake success, until the backup key source is decided. The server now maps `ErrKeyExists` to its RPC code; before, it fell through to Internal. Files: `xkey/pkg/pairing/bridge_{oath,piv,sync,backup}.go`, `bridge.go`, `errors.go`, `protocol.go`, `xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/device_listen.go`; `oath.GenerateCredentialID` and `sync.Checksum` are exported. Verified by per-method round trips through `Bridge.HandleRequest`, and by `device_listen_collaborators_test.go`, where an OATH add and a trust-store sync through the listen-built bridge persist to the real on-disk stores.
- **`xkey fido2` with the phone backend now serves the same OATH, PIV and sync bridge methods as `xkey device listen`** (#1041). `connectXKMSdBridge` (`xkey/cmd/xkey/cmd/fido2_phone_bridge.go`) used to build its own `pairing.BridgeConfig` with only TPM enrollment wired, so a phone paired through it got `ErrorCodeFeatureUnavailable` for those methods. It now calls the same `buildListenBridgeConfig` as `device listen`, and closes the collaborators on shutdown. Verified by `fido2_phone_bridge_collaborators_test.go`.
- **The PKCS#11 module now reaches the running xkey through the same socket resolution as every xkey command** (#1038). `xkey/pkg/pkcs11/ipc_transport.go` hard-coded `~/.xkey/run/xkey.sock`, so with `XKEY_HOME` unset it looked somewhere other than where the daemon listened, and it couldn't be pointed at one of several instances. It now uses `ipc.DefaultSocketPath()`: `XKEY_IPC_SOCKET`, then `<XKEY_HOME>/run/xkey.sock`, then the XDG default. Verified by `ipc_transport_test.go`.
- **Fixed a data race between the standalone TrustedCA's `Serve` and `Shutdown` on the tenant rate limiter** (#706). `Serve` assigned `tca.tenantRateLimiter` without holding `tca.mu`. `Shutdown`, which a caller may invoke while `Serve`'s setup is still running, reads and clears it under that lock. The limiter is now built locally and published under `tca.mu`, matching `restService` and `acmeServer` in the same function (`pkg/acme/client/trustedca.go`). Found by a new `-race` test that drives a real HTTPS request through the tenant-auth and rate-limit middleware.

## [0.31.0-alpha] - 2026-09-25

### Security

- **xkey now refuses AWS credentials that could inject keys or profiles into `~/.aws/credentials`, and replaces the file atomically with mode `0600`.** `xkey/pkg/oidc/handlers/aws_credentials.go` wrote the token endpoint's `AccessKeyID`, `SecretAccessKey` and `SessionToken` (and the region and profile name) as `key = value` lines without checking them, so a hostile or tampered response carrying a newline could add a `credential_process = <cmd>` key, which the AWS CLI and SDKs execute, or a whole `[profile]` section. `AWSCredentialsHandler.Handle` now validates every value before it touches the disk and refuses, never sanitises: the access key ID must be 16 to 128 bytes of `A-Z 0-9`; the secret printable ASCII with no whitespace or controls; the session token the base64 alphabet `A-Z a-z 0-9 + / =`; the profile name `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - @ + : /`; the region `a-z 0-9 -`. Refusals return new typed sentinels (`ErrAWSInvalidAccessKeyID`, `ErrAWSInvalidSecretAccessKey`, `ErrAWSInvalidSessionToken`, `ErrAWSInvalidProfile`, `ErrAWSInvalidRegion`) wrapped in `DetailError` with the length or byte offset, never the value, and leave the existing file byte-for-byte unchanged. The write now `fsync`s the temporary file and the directory around the rename, sets `0600` on the temporary file before writing, removes it on any failure, and propagates every write error that was previously discarded. Other profiles are kept as before; output is now deterministic (profiles and extra keys in name order), and `aws_credential_expiration` is formatted in UTC instead of local time with a literal `Z`. No other INI or env-file writer in `xkey/pkg` or `xkey/cmd` formats untrusted values: the SoftHSM2 config template takes only a path under `$HOME`, and the exec handler passes environment entries through `execve`, not a file. Docs: `xkey/docs/oidc/engineering.md`, `xkey/docs/oidc/cli.md`. Verified by `xkey/pkg/oidc/handlers/aws_credentials_validate_test.go` (`\n`, `\r`, `[`, `=` and NUL in each field and the profile and region are refused with the file unchanged and no temporary file left; real-shaped STS credentials round-trip with other profiles preserved and mode `0600`; rule bounds; rename-failure cleanup), with `HOME` and `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` redirected into `t.TempDir()`. go-xkms#1020.
- **xkey no longer passes identity-provider text to the terminal or logs
  as raw control sequences.**
  A hostile or compromised identity provider could put ANSI/OSC escape
  sequences in the callback's `error` and `error_description`, in a
  token-endpoint error, or in an ID-token claim. xkey printed and logged
  that text unchanged, so the provider could clear the screen, spoof a
  prompt or write the clipboard through OSC 52. All such text now passes
  through one function, `oidc.SanitizeProviderText`, before it reaches a
  terminal or a log. The function removes every ESC-introduced and 8-bit C1
  sequence whole and drops the remaining C0/C1 controls and bidi overrides.
  It turns line breaks into spaces, so a provider cannot forge a log line,
  and it cuts the text to 512 bytes, marking the cut with `...[truncated]`.
  It is applied to the CLI, GUI and `xkey oidc aws` callback errors, to
  `oidc.TokenRequestError.Error()`, to the AWS token-request error, to the
  GUI's refresh error, and to the claims and AWS access key ID that
  `xkey oidc login`, `xkey oidc token` and `xkey oidc aws login` print.
  Tests send an OSC 52 + `ESC[2J` + 8-bit CSI + NUL payload through every
  one of these paths and assert that it comes out as plain text. A fuzz
  target checks that the output is inert, bounded and idempotent.
  (go-xkms#1015)

### Fixed

- **The last ignored errors in library and CLI code are handled, and the
  bugs they were hiding are fixed.**
  - The REST `page`/`page_size` query parameters now return 400 when they
    are not numeric. All eight paged REST list endpoints (crypto backends,
    keys, certificates, custodian groups, shares, tenants, FROST keys, PIV
    slots) now parse pagination through the one shared
    `transport.PageRequestFromQuery` implementation
    (`pkg/api/transport/pagination.go`) instead of a REST-local
    `parsePageRequest` duplicate that built its errors with `fmt.Errorf`;
    the shared function's `*InvalidPaginationParamError` is a typed error.
    `sort_order` now also accepts the `asc`/`desc` string form the REST API
    and its TypeScript SDK send on the wire, in addition to the existing
    integer form, so the two implementations agree on what is valid. The
    query parameters and the 400 are documented in the `api.md` of every
    affected feature folder (crypto-backends, key-management,
    certificate-authority, share-custody, frost-threshold-signing,
    piv-smartcard, multi-tenancy); three of those folders
    (piv-smartcard, multi-tenancy, share-custody) previously said their
    lists were unpaged or "returned whole", which stopped being true once
    pagination landed on those handlers. The TypeScript SDK's `PageQuery`
    doc comment now says `page`/`page_size` must be integers.
  - `ExecHandler` (`xkey oidc ... --output exec --pass-json`) no longer
    reports a command that exited 0 as failed. A child that exits without
    reading all of a large (>64 KiB) JSON payload on stdin makes the
    write's goroutine observe `EPIPE`, or the following `Close` observe
    `os.ErrClosed`; both are now filtered out as benign instead of being
    joined into the result.
  - `xkey oidc stop` no longer reports a PID file that was never created as
    a removal failure; only a removal failure other than `os.ErrNotExist`
    is surfaced.
  - `xkey barrier`'s PCR-policy auto-unseal no longer turns a successful
    auto-unseal into a failure when closing the PCR policy store
    afterward fails; that failure is logged instead, matching the
    documented `(true, closer, nil)` success contract.
  - The OIDC client bounds every token-endpoint response read to 1 MiB
    (`io.LimitReader`) instead of an unbounded `io.ReadAll`, and a
    non-OAuth2 error body is truncated to 256 bytes, stripped of
    non-printable characters, and prefixed with the status code and
    content type before it reaches `TokenRequestError.Description`.
  - `xkey piv status` no longer turns a failure closing PIV storage into a
    command failure; that command's job is to report status ("don't fail,
    just report status" is already its convention for every other error in
    it), so the close failure is now warned on the output writer instead,
    matching `xkey migrate`'s existing warning convention.
  - Malformed share, custodian and tenant timestamps on the gRPC and unix
    transports are logged instead of silently becoming zero.
  - `xkey oath generate` warns when it cannot persist an advanced HOTP
    counter, so the counter can no longer drift silently.
  - The `e2eprobe` interop probe no longer treats an undecodable response as
    an empty success.

  Across the root module and xkey, cleanup errors are joined into the
  returned error, or logged where the function has no error channel. The
  join happens only when Close actually fails, so bare sentinel returns keep
  their identity -- including at the sites a follow-up review found still
  joining unconditionally (`barrier_init.go`, `barrier_seal.go`,
  `barrier_unseal.go`, `secret_service.go`, `device_pair.go`, `barrier.go`,
  `barrier_auto_unseal.go`, `xkey/pkg/oidc/callback.go`,
  `xkey/pkg/keyboard/keyboard.go`, `xkey/pkg/nativemsg/pairing.go`), which
  are now guarded the same way. What remains is CLI output writes,
  flag-binding calls, read-side body closes, and discards of non-error
  values. (go-xkms#701)
- **TPM ECC encryption keys can do ECDH, and TPM auth errors are classified
  correctly.** `CreateECDSA` never set `Sign` or `Decrypt`, so every ECC key
  it created was sign-only and `ECDHZGen` could never succeed through the
  public API. `KeyTypeEncryption`/`KeyTypeEncapsulation` now produce a
  Decrypt, non-Sign template (scheme `TPM_ALG_NULL`), mirroring `CreateRSA`.
  `isTPMAuthError`'s typed path masked the response code with `0x0FF`, which
  never matched format-1 `BAD_AUTH`/`AUTH_FAIL` codes, so the function worked
  only through string matching. It and `isTPMBadAuth` now classify with
  `errors.Is(err, tpm2.TPMRC...)` (go-tpm's `TPMRC.Is`). (go-xkms#1003,
  #1004)

## [0.30.0-alpha] - 2026-09-25

### Security

- **xkey's OIDC callback page no longer renders the provider's error as
  HTML.**
  The CLI's loopback callback page wrote the `error` and `error_description`
  query parameters into its HTML unescaped, so anyone able to steer the
  browser to the callback URL while a login was pending (a hostile IdP, a
  crafted link) could inject markup or script into the local callback
  origin. Every callback page (CLI, GUI and `xkey oidc aws`) is now rendered
  by one function, `oidc.WriteCallbackPage`, through `html/template`, and is
  served with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`,
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src
  'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
  Tests send a `<script>` / `"><img onerror>` redirect to each of the three
  handlers and assert the escaped output and the headers. (go-xkms#1013)

### Added

- **PCR policy management now works over every network transport, not just
  REST.** `PolicyCreate`, `PolicyGet`, `PolicyList`, `PolicyDelete`,
  `PolicyRefresh`, `PolicyVerify` and `PolicyExport` were `ErrNotSupported`
  one-liners on the gRPC, Unix, QUIC and MCP client transports, and
  `PasswordStoreSetAccessMode` was likewise stubbed on gRPC and Unix
  (go-xkms#691); `xkmsctl policy` and any SDK caller not on REST failed on
